{
  "project_id": "P-SLE-ConnectivityAgMarketInfra",
  "risks": [
    {
      "risk_id": "R01",
      "description": "Severe flooding during construction could damage bridge foundations and delay works.",
      "category": "environmental",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 5,
      "mitigation": "Apply flood‑resilient design, schedule critical works outside peak rainy season, and install temporary cofferdams.",
      "evidence": "Component 2.1 description of flood‑adaptation measures for bridges (Annex 5)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R02",
      "description": "Extreme heat may cause premature deterioration of road and bridge pavements.",
      "category": "environmental",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Use heat‑resistant materials, incorporate expansion joints, and specify thermal design limits in specifications.",
      "evidence": "Annex 5 climate‑adaptation measures mention weather‑resistant materials for bridges and roads."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R03",
      "description": "Fragmented institutional responsibilities could lead to coordination failures among ministries and agencies.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Strengthen NPSC oversight, define clear roles in the Project Implementation Manual, and hold monthly coordination meetings.",
      "evidence": "Section 15 notes institutional fragmentation and overlapping responsibilities."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R04",
      "description": "The PCIU lacks an established procurement unit and qualified staff, risking ineffective procurement.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Recruit qualified procurement specialists before effectiveness, provide World Bank procurement training, and set up a record‑keeping system.",
      "evidence": "Annex 6 procurement risk assessment: “PCIU is yet to be established and the capacity of procurement staff… low.”"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R05",
      "description": "MTA’s limited experience with World Bank financial‑management procedures may cause compliance gaps.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Hire a FM specialist, develop a FM manual, and conduct targeted FM training for staff.",
      "evidence": "Annex 7 FM assessment cites “Insufficient experience of MTA with the World Bank’s FM procedures.”"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R06",
      "description": "A US$7.1 million financing gap for four SCADeP bridges could postpone their completion.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Secure the GoSL’s pledged fiscal contribution, explore private‑sector bridge financing, and activate contingency funds if needed.",
      "evidence": "Component 2 sub‑component b description of the US$7.1 m gap and GoSL commitment."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R07",
      "description": "Prolonged rainy seasons may suspend civil works, extending the project schedule.",
      "category": "schedule",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Adopt incremental launching construction method, build weather buffers into the timeline, and monitor forecasts closely.",
      "evidence": "Section 9 notes the incremental launching method to avoid delays from rainy seasons."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R08",
      "description": "Corruption or fraud in procurement could inflate costs and undermine project integrity.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 5,
      "mitigation": "Implement transparent bidding, use STEP for monitoring, enforce anti‑corruption training, and conduct regular PPRs.",
      "evidence": "Annex 6 lists fraud and corruption risks and mitigation measures."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R09",
      "description": "Limited competition in tendering may lead to higher prices and lower quality.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Aggregate small packages, run outreach to private sector, and publish clear tender documents.",
      "evidence": "Annex 6 procurement risk assessment mentions “Insufficient competition in procurement.”"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R10",
      "description": "Absence of a systematic road‑safety database hampers evidence‑based safety policy.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Develop a national road‑safety information system and integrate data collection into the RAMS platform.",
      "evidence": "Section 8 states “There is no systematic database on road safety.”"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R11",
      "description": "Gender gaps may limit women’s access to transport services and market facilities.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Incorporate gender‑sensitive design (lighting, sidewalks, women‑only spaces), set hiring targets, and run outreach through women’s groups.",
      "evidence": "Gender sections describe gender‑informed designs for components 1‑3."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R12",
      "description": "Low mobile‑phone penetration among rural women could reduce uptake of the AMIS mobile app.",
      "category": "external",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Provide community‑based information channels, conduct digital‑literacy trainings, and use radio/TV to disseminate market data.",
      "evidence": "Section on AMIS notes limited phone access for rural women and need for alternative channels."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R13",
      "description": "Insufficient post‑completion funding may jeopardize bridge and road maintenance.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 5,
      "mitigation": "Establish bridge management system with cost‑recovery mechanisms, train local councils on revenue collection, and embed O&M budgets in RMFA.",
      "evidence": "Critical Assumption 2: “Funding is available and project bridges and link roads are adequately maintained after project closing.”"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R14",
      "description": "Increased flood frequency could cause scour around bridge piers, threatening structural integrity.",
      "category": "environmental",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 5,
      "mitigation": "Design with right‑sized drains, install scour protection, and schedule regular underwater inspections.",
      "evidence": "Component 2.1 design includes scour protection and flood‑resilient standards."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R15",
      "description": "Unclear CERC activation procedures may delay emergency response funding.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Finalize CERC manual and Emergency Action Plan before implementation, train staff on trigger criteria.",
      "evidence": "Component 5 description of CERC and need for manual."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R16",
      "description": "Delay in establishing the National Project Steering Committee could weaken project oversight.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Meet the 60‑day covenant, allocate resources, and appoint members promptly after effectiveness.",
      "evidence": "Legal covenants schedule 2, Section I.A.2(a) require NPSC within 60 days."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R17",
      "description": "Inadequate climate data may lead to under‑designed flood protection for bridges.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Use climate‑proofed design parameters, update flood quantification methods, and apply safety factors.",
      "evidence": "Annex 5 notes need to factor climate change into design flood levels."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R18",
      "description": "Bus fleet expansion may not keep pace with rising urban travel demand, worsening congestion.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Implement lease‑operate‑own scheme, prioritize bus lanes, and regularly update demand forecasts.",
      "evidence": "Component 1 sub‑component c describes fleet renewal and demand growth to 750,000 trips/day by 2033."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R19",
      "description": "If market infrastructure is delayed, post‑harvest losses could remain high, reducing farmer incomes.",
      "category": "schedule",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Fast‑track construction, monitor milestones weekly, and allocate contingency funds for critical path items.",
      "evidence": "Component 3 notes post‑harvest losses of 20‑30 % and need for timely market upgrades."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R20",
      "description": "Sexual harassment incidents on public transport may deter women’s use of services.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Install CCTV on buses, set up a hotline, conduct SH awareness training for operators.",
      "evidence": "Component 1 sub‑component c mentions CCTV and SH response measures."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R21",
      "description": "Weak grievance redress mechanisms could lead to community dissatisfaction and project delays.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Establish a transparent GRM, publicize procedures, and ensure timely response within set timelines.",
      "evidence": "Section V outlines Grievance Redress Services."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R22",
      "description": "High inflation and fiscal pressures may erode real project costs and affect budgeting.",
      "category": "external",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Include cost‑escalation clauses, monitor macro‑economic indicators, and adjust budgets annually.",
      "evidence": "Country Context notes “soaring inflation driven by global supply shocks” and fiscal pressures."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R23",
      "description": "Limited capacity of local contractors may affect construction quality and timelines.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Conduct pre‑qualification, provide technical training, and assign qualified supervision consultants.",
      "evidence": "Annex 6 procurement risk assessment cites “lack of knowledge in using World Bank’s Procurement Regulations.”"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R24",
      "description": "Zero‑emission bus technology may be infeasible, limiting GHG mitigation benefits.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Perform feasibility study, adopt hybrid or high‑efficiency diesel buses if electric not viable, and revisit later.",
      "evidence": "Component 1 notes bus fleet may use zero‑emission or hybrid buses if technically feasible."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R25",
      "description": "Weak data management for BMS/RAMS could impair asset‑management decisions.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Develop GIS‑based BMS, train staff, and integrate with RAMS for real‑time monitoring.",
      "evidence": "Component 2 sub‑component c describes establishment of climate‑resilient BMS."
    }
  ]
}

risks.description: Severe flooding during construction could damage bridge foundations and delay works.
risks.mitigation: Apply flood‑resilient design, schedule critical works outside peak rainy season, and install temporary cofferdams.
risks.evidence: Component 2.1 description of flood‑adaptation measures for bridges (Annex 5).

risks.description: Extreme heat may cause premature deterioration of road and bridge pavements.
risks.mitigation: Use heat‑resistant materials, incorporate expansion joints, and specify thermal design limits in specifications.
risks.evidence: Annex 5 climate‑adaptation measures mention weather‑resistant materials for bridges and roads.

risks.description: Fragmented institutional responsibilities could lead to coordination failures among ministries and agencies.
risks.mitigation: Strengthen NPSC oversight, define clear roles in the Project Implementation Manual, and hold monthly coordination meetings.
risks.evidence: Section 15 notes institutional fragmentation and overlapping responsibilities.

risks.description: The PCIU lacks an established procurement unit and qualified staff, risking ineffective procurement.
risks.mitigation: Recruit qualified procurement specialists before effectiveness, provide World Bank procurement training, and set up a record‑keeping system.
risks.evidence: Annex 6 procurement risk assessment: “PCIU is yet to be established and the capacity of procurement staff… low.”

risks.description: MTA’s limited experience with World Bank financial‑management procedures may cause compliance gaps.
risks.mitigation: Hire a FM specialist, develop a FM manual, and conduct targeted FM training for staff.
risks.evidence: Annex 7 FM assessment cites “Insufficient experience of MTA with the World Bank’s FM procedures.”

risks.description: A US$7.1 million financing gap for four SCADeP bridges could postpone their completion.
risks.mitigation: Secure the GoSL’s pledged fiscal contribution, explore private‑sector bridge financing, and activate contingency funds if needed.
risks.evidence: Component 2 sub‑component b description of the US$7.1 m gap and GoSL commitment.

risks.description: Prolonged rainy seasons may suspend civil works, extending the project schedule.
risks.mitigation: Adopt incremental launching construction method, build weather buffers into the timeline, and monitor forecasts closely.
risks.evidence: Section 9 notes the incremental launching method to avoid delays from rainy seasons.

risks.description: Corruption or fraud in procurement could inflate costs and undermine project integrity.
risks.mitigation: Implement transparent bidding, use STEP for monitoring, enforce anti‑corruption training, and conduct regular PPRs.
risks.evidence: Annex 6 lists fraud and corruption risks and mitigation measures.

risks.description: Limited competition in tendering may lead to higher prices and lower quality.
risks.mitigation: Aggregate small packages, run outreach to private sector, and publish clear tender documents.
risks.evidence: Annex 6 procurement risk assessment mentions “Insufficient competition in procurement.”

risks.description: Absence of a systematic road‑safety database hampers evidence‑based safety policy.
risks.mitigation: Develop a national road‑safety information system and integrate data collection into the RAMS platform.
risks.evidence: Section 8 states “There is no systematic database on road safety.”

risks.description: Gender gaps may limit women’s access to transport services and market facilities.
risks.mitigation: Incorporate gender‑sensitive design (lighting, sidewalks, women‑only spaces), set hiring targets, and run outreach through women’s groups.
risks.evidence: Gender sections describe gender‑informed designs for components 1‑3.

risks.description: Low mobile‑phone penetration among rural women could reduce uptake of the AMIS mobile app.
risks.mitigation: Provide community‑based information channels, conduct digital‑literacy trainings, and use radio/TV to disseminate market data.
risks.evidence: Section on AMIS notes limited phone access for rural women and need for alternative channels.

risks.description: Insufficient post‑completion funding may jeopardize bridge and road maintenance.
risks.mitigation: Establish bridge management system with cost‑recovery mechanisms, train local councils on revenue collection, and embed O&M budgets in RMFA.
risks.evidence: Critical Assumption 2: “Funding is available and project bridges and link roads are adequately maintained after project closing.”

risks.description: Increased flood frequency could cause scour around bridge piers, threatening structural integrity.
risks.mitigation: Design with right‑sized drains, install scour protection, and schedule regular underwater inspections.
risks.evidence: Component 2.1 design includes scour protection and flood‑resilient standards.

risks.description: Unclear CERC activation procedures may delay emergency response funding.
risks.mitigation: Finalize CERC manual and Emergency Action Plan before implementation, train staff on trigger criteria.
risks.evidence: Component 5 description of CERC and need for manual.

risks.description: Delay in establishing the National Project Steering Committee could weaken project oversight.
risks.mitigation: Meet the 60‑day covenant, allocate resources, and appoint members promptly after effectiveness.
risks.evidence: Legal covenants schedule 2, Section I.A.2(a) require NPSC within 60 days.

risks.description: Inadequate climate data may lead to under‑designed flood protection for bridges.
risks.mitigation: Use climate‑proofed design parameters, update flood quantification methods, and apply safety factors.
risks.evidence: Annex 5 notes need to factor climate change into design flood levels.

risks.description: Bus fleet expansion may not keep pace with rising urban travel demand, worsening congestion.
risks.mitigation: Implement lease‑operate‑own scheme, prioritize bus lanes, and regularly update demand forecasts.
risks.evidence: Component 1 sub‑component c describes fleet renewal and demand growth to 750,000 trips/day by 2033.

risks.description: If market infrastructure is delayed, post‑harvest losses could remain high, reducing farmer incomes.
risks.mitigation: Fast‑track construction, monitor milestones weekly, and allocate contingency funds for critical path items.
risks.evidence: Component 3 notes post‑harvest losses of 20‑30 % and need for timely market upgrades.

risks.description: Sexual harassment incidents on public transport may deter women’s use of services.
risks.mitigation: Install CCTV on buses, set up a hotline, conduct SH awareness training for operators.
risks.evidence: Component 1 sub‑component c mentions CCTV and SH response measures.

risks.description: Weak grievance redress mechanisms could lead to community dissatisfaction and project delays.
risks.mitigation: Establish a transparent GRM, publicize procedures, and ensure timely response within set timelines.
risks.evidence: Section V outlines Grievance Redress Services.

risks.description: High inflation and fiscal pressures may erode real project costs and affect budgeting.
risks.mitigation: Include cost‑escalation clauses, monitor macro‑economic indicators, and adjust budgets annually.
risks.evidence: Country Context notes “soaring inflation driven by global supply shocks” and fiscal pressures.

risks.description: Limited capacity of local contractors may affect construction quality and timelines.
risks.mitigation: Conduct pre‑qualification, provide technical training, and assign qualified supervision consultants.
risks.evidence: Annex 6 procurement risk assessment cites “lack of knowledge in using World Bank’s Procurement Regulations.”

risks.description: Zero‑emission bus technology may be infeasible, limiting GHG mitigation benefits.
risks.mitigation: Perform feasibility study, adopt hybrid or high‑efficiency diesel buses if electric not viable, and revisit later.
risks.evidence: Component 1 notes bus fleet may use zero‑emission or hybrid buses if technically feasible.

risks.description: Weak data management for BMS/RAMS could impair asset‑management decisions.
risks.mitigation: Develop GIS‑based BMS, train staff, and integrate with RAMS for real‑time monitoring.
risks.evidence: Component 2 sub‑component c describes establishment of climate‑resilient BMS.
